item.aggregated_output:
# Storyboard — The ferment log

Status: complete planning proposal, awaiting storyboard review. Nothing built. Concept selected under F24's delegation. Chapter titles are navigation labels and working titles, not final marketing copy.

## Pending inputs, with safe defaults

1. Actual personal photograph files: use a fully typographic log until supplied. Ownership is confirmed, but no photographs have been inspected. Exclude prices and unapproved faces, including those in reflections or backgrounds. A restaurant log excerpt needs clearance; its absence does not block the design.
2. Actual workshop booking URL and public enquiry address: needed before launch. No invented addresses, live booking buttons or suggestion of current apprentice vacancies. Use enquiry wording until a real application route is confirmed.
3. Restaurant permission for Priya's photographs and Olu's permission for drawings: optional later enhancements only; neither is planned into the core scenes. Credit Priya Nair wherever an approved photograph appears. No Brine scan that includes Olu's work without his permission.
4. Unanswered figures and role details stay out: 40 seats, 40+ rotation, annual apprentice count, 90 covers, supplier reduction and detailed Sunday Pot case study. No inferred impact story or explanation of overlapping employment dates. Existing-site migration remains unspecified.

## Direction

Question: **What happens before the menu is written?**

One continuous scroll follows six leaves of a ferment log. The log's confirmed fields provide the sequence: started, salt, checks, readiness. Review and Next batch are editorial extensions, not claimed real headings. The ending answers through the order of the evidence: prep and recorded checks precede readiness, and the menu is written last. This is an editorial arrangement of confirmed facts, not a claim that the log caused the waste reduction.

The six leaves remain on screen throughout the enhanced desktop experience, even when five gather beside the active leaf. Paper geometry is simple. Faces contain meaningful words, source images or data; no independent spectacle, floating food, particle field, rotating chef emblem or fake kitchen simulation. Renderings are clearly designed representations, not counterfeit scans of her notebook. No made-up salt percentages, dates or food-safety guidance.

## Chapters

| Chapter | Name in the form | Role | What it tells | What the pieces do | What you can touch |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Started | Opening, who, where from | Ines, Saltmarsh, Leeds; influences; ten-week stage; Head Chef from September 2022 | Open log becomes a short dated fan, with influence leaf separate from chronology | Jump links, contact skip, expand concise background |
| 2 | Salt | How | The named log fields and prep list; no invented recipe | Leaves align as a field diagram, one face per field | Tap or focus a field to highlight its matching text; all explanations remain visible |
| 3 | Checks | How and work | Checking recorded in the log; apprentice programme and preserving zine | Leaves become an aligned working spread linking checks to the broader teaching/writing practice | Accessible links to text details; no hover-only facts |
| 4 | Ready | Work in view | Larder and preserving practice; workshop pathway | Same six leaves form a loose contact sheet, active image larger, others visible | Open supplied personal photos in an accessible lightbox; workshop jump |
| 5 | Review | Outcomes and others' words | Whole-kitchen waste measure and Callum's quotation | Two leaves sit side by side for 14 and 5; next leaf turns to quotation | Measurement note and credits visible in HTML |
| 6 | Next batch | Answer and contact | Menu-last practice; three ways to take part | Leaves settle back into one open log; final leaf finishes the sequence | Workshop booking/enquiry, apprentice enquiry, writer enquiry |

## Beats

Screen allocations are approximate desktop viewport heights with native scrolling, about 9.5 total. They are not mandatory dwell times. Text may increase height; phones use content height. Motion occupies the transition between readable settled states, without trapping scrolling.

| Chapter / beat | Screens | How the same pieces stand | What is on their faces | What the chapter adds | Caption working title and fact basis |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Started / arrival | 1 | Six leaves in one open, slightly staggered log | Identity and question on lead leaf; personal pot photograph if supplied, otherwise names of influences; log fields on other leaves | HTML identity, brief proof and three contact shortcuts; no loading gate | Before the menu — F01, F04, F05, F15, F20, F21, F23 |
| Started / background | 1 | Three leaves fan into a compact dated sequence; three remain gathered | Named books/grandmother on influence leaf; stage duties on one; acting role March 2022 and Head Chef September 2022 on another | Optional expanded background text, kept concise | Influences and practice — F04, F10, F15; no invented connection between these events |
| Salt / fields | 1.25 | Four leaves align as log columns; two hold the edge | Exact supplied field names: date started, salt, days checked, ready; prep-list title on fifth; no sample values | Readable HTML field list and prep-list context | What the log records — F23 |
| Checks / working spread | 1.25 | Leaves pair into three spreads | Checking-field names; apprentice programme; Brine title and preserving subject, typographic only | Short text about named activities without unconfirmed duties, targets or curriculum | Checking, teaching, writing — F03, F13, F23 |
| Ready / work contact sheet | 1.25 | Six leaves form a compact, irregular grid | Personal larder photo, detail from the same photo if useful, pot image, and text leaves for log, Brine and workshops; no claim of six distinct projects | Accessible work index using only safe facts; image credits | Work in view — F03, F14, F18, F20, F23 |
| Review / measurement | 1 | Two leaves square to viewer; four remain stacked beside them | 14 kg/week and 5 kg/week, equally sized type; whole-kitchen attribution and 2023 measurement note | Scope: prep and plate waste, weighed over one month; bones excluded because used for stock | What we measured — F05; use “we”; do not say ongoing, individual or caused by log |
| Review / quotation | 0.75 | Quotation leaf moves forward; evidence leaves remain visible behind | Callum's exact supplied quote and name/role | No star rating or invented publication logo | Callum's words — F16 |
| Next batch / close | 2 | All leaves return to one open log, final leaf turns once then rests | Prep/log/menu order and three audience routes; a designed menu title only, no fabricated dish list | Complete contact block; credit/accessibility/footer links | Menu last — F21, F23; contact destination pending |

These are beat specifications, not final captions. Opening prose and all new narrative copy remain to be written and reviewed later. The approved direct quotation is preserved exactly.

## Thirty-second visit

The first screen contains Ines Okafor, Head Chef at Saltmarsh in Leeds, the fermentation/apprentice focus, and compact proof: the kitchen's 14-to-5 kg/week result with the 2023 one-month scope adjacent. Keep proof in ordinary HTML rather than microscopic log text. A discreet rail names the six chapters and has a skip-to-contact link. Workshop, apprentice and writer routes are accessible immediately. Visitors can reach the right destination without completing the animation.

## Appearance

Selected default: **Working paper**. Warm paper ground #F2EBDD; near-black ink #242821; dark olive accent #495B38; leaves #FFFCF4. Fine ruled lines, restrained paper grain and believable shallow shadows. No artificial coffee stains, handwriting font or manufactured ageing. Olive is for links and focus details; text contrast must be checked during implementation.

Alternatives retained for later review, not separate concepts:

| Look | Ground | Ink | Accent | Piece surface |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Working paper — selected | #F2EBDD | #242821 | #495B38 | Warm, almost-white ruled paper |
| Fresh ledger | #F4F4EE | #242C31 | #345F78 | Cool ivory leaves, blue-grey rules |
| Evening desk | #22271F | #F4EFDF | #D7B56D | Warm ivory leaves with dark printed type; dark surrounding desk |

The alternatives derive from paper and ink; they are not invented claims about Saltmarsh's decor. If built later, review them on the same scroll. Do not add a visitor-facing theme selector by default.

Two self-hosted, open-license typefaces: **Source Serif 4** for headings and reading text; **IBM Plex Mono** for printed log fields, dates, measurements and small navigation labels. Serif provides a publishing voice for Ines's writing; mono gives the log orderly, readable columns. Use actual font weights, keep prose about 60–68 characters wide, body at least 18px where space permits, and avoid all-caps paragraphs. On phones the identity and question scale down fluidly. No important text exists only in a texture.

## Motion and interaction

Native vertical scrolling drives modest leaf translation, rotation and regrouping. No scroll hijacking, forced pauses, continuous idle spinning, automatic sound or pointer-chasing camera. Desktop uses a sticky scene with adjacent HTML text; exits from sticky regions must work with browser history, anchors and keyboard navigation. A leaf settles before the next block needs reading. Hover can emphasize a face but exposes no unique content. Clicking a work entry opens standard accessible content, never requires rotating an object.

| Context | Experience and substitute for 3D |
|---|---|
| Phone | Default static two-dimensional leaves above each text section, maintaining the same six-chapter order. No pinned canvas or multi-screen empty scroll. Stacked photo figures, a compact chapter menu, large contact buttons, minimum 44px touch targets. Result columns stack if needed. All work and proof remain. |
| Reduced motion | Static settled compositions per chapter; immediate navigation and no parallax, camera travel, leaf turning or animated number counting. |
| No WebGL / context lost | Replace canvas with prepared stills or CSS/HTML leaf arrangements; preserve scroll position and all links. No error dialog required to read. |
| No JavaScript | Server-rendered or static HTML with the complete chapter text, images, native anchors and contact destinations; static log illustrations. Native detail elements may hold optional background. |

Canvas is decorative to assistive technology because an equivalent ordered semantic document carries every fact, image description and relationship. Provide skip link, logical heading order, visible keyboard focus, alt text, sufficient contrast, and no colour-only meanings. Mobile layouts must survive zoom and long text.

Performance plan for future implementation: load readable HTML and the lead still first; lazy-load desktop 3D after primary content, load only needed font subsets, use compressed responsive images, cap canvas pixel density, and stop rendering offscreen. Reuse six simple sheet meshes and a small texture atlas; no large restaurant model. Aim for LCP under 2.5 seconds and CLS under 0.1 on representative mobile testing, with no 3D bundle in the default mobile path. These are targets, not measured results.

## Everything else

Here “Build” means include in a future implementation after approval; it does not authorize coding now. All scope choices below made by assistant under F24 unless marked user.

| Item | Build, later or never | Decision and reason |
|---|---|---|
| Way round the page | Build | Named chapter rail, mobile menu, native anchors, contact skip and browser back support; assistant |
| Page for each project | Later | No thin case-study pages without enough cleared material; assistant |
| Every project listed | Build, safe subset | Inline index for larder, apprentice programme, Brine and workshops. Hold Sunday Pot detail pending personal duties and story boundaries; assistant |
| How to reach Ines | Build | Three clear routes using actual supplied destinations; workshops primary, apprentices second, writers third. No unconfirmed open-vacancy wording; assistant based on user audiences |
| CV | Never for this scope | User is not job seeking; concise background suffices; assistant |
| What others say | Build | Callum's exact cleared quotation, attributed once; user clearance, assistant placement |
| Languages | Build English; later others | English supplied; no assumed translations; assistant |
| Shared link and icon | Build | Name, role, location and log-derived image; icon from log ruling, not copied art. Metadata, canonical URL, sitemap and social image; assistant |
| Missing-address page | Build | Plain message and links to start, workshops and contact; assistant |
| Blog | Later | Brine remains in the work index; no empty publication schedule; assistant |
| Chat | Never | No established visitor need; assistant |
| Legal/privacy notices | Build as applicable | UK requirements reviewed against actual site operator and data collection at implementation. Minimal data handling; disclose any form service. Avoid nonessential trackers by default; assistant |
| Credits | Build | Visible image credits and a compact credit list; Priya credit required if her images are later cleared; user/assistant |
| Booking integration | Build external link first | Use existing service if one exists; no payment system or invented availability; assistant |
| Content maintenance | Build | Simple editable content for workshop links, contact, proof notes and image credits; a separate CMS is later only if needed; assistant |
| Testing | Build-stage work | Keyboard/zoom/reduced motion/no-JS/no-WebGL, phone layouts, link targets, contrast, performance and rights/claim review; assistant |

## Decisions to review

Chose log over prep slips and tags; chose paper/olive over cool ledger and evening desk; chose serif body plus monospaced log labels; kept a single page and a short background; prioritised workshops then apprenticeship and writer enquiries; chose static mobile and accessible equivalents; excluded unresolved claims and third-party artwork; deferred blog, CMS and individual case-study pages. Each can change without revising source facts.

Review request: approve this storyboard or identify changes to its concept, sequence, appearance or contact priorities. No implementation follows automatically from approval; this skill's scope ends at an approved plan.
# Planning handover

Read both supplied files: material/notes.md and material/linkedin.md.

Created facts.md, concepts.md, storyboard.md and decided-for-you.md. No website code created.

Current stage: Storyfolio stop 3, storyboard awaiting review. User requests full portfolio planning, including idea, scroll sequence, content, colours, typography, mobile and supporting needs; explicitly no building.

User answered core factual questions and explicitly delegated remaining choices. Answers recorded beside affected facts, with new facts F21–F24. Resolved title date: acting March 2022; Head Chef September 2022. Waste: whole-kitchen prep and plate waste, 14 to 5 kg weekly, weighed over one month in 2023; bones excluded. Stage: unpaid, ten weeks, jars/labels and two garum batches, not research. Callum quotation cleared; Olu drawings pending; restaurant owns Priya photos and her credit is required. Personal photo files are not yet supplied.

Read concept.md, asking.md and storyboard.md. Developed three distinct form/object options and chose The ferment log under user delegation. Storyboard includes six chapters, eight beats, looks, type, audience routes, fallbacks, supporting scope, pending inputs and assumptions. Storyboard approval has not been received.

Next: record approval or revisions. Do not ask the user to reselect a concept unless they wish to change it. Do not write final captions yet, invent unanswered facts, assume third-party rights or build. After storyboard approval, update this handover and state that implementation is outside this planning skill's scope.

item.text:
The direction is **The ferment log**, built around one question: **What happens before the menu is written?**

The complete plan is saved in [storyboard.md](/tmp/storyfolio-evals/codex-chef-with-0bOu0J/docs/story/storyboard.md). Nothing has been built. This planning phase ends with the specification below.

**The idea and the continuous object**

Visitors follow the work that precedes your menu: preparation, recording, checking, readiness and teaching. The menu appears at the end because that is where it belongs in your actual working week.

One object carries the entire experience: **six paper leaves of a ferment log**. As visitors scroll, the same leaves open, separate into fields, become a photographic display, present evidence and return to one document.

Six is a design choice, not a claim about your actual log. The representation uses your field names and confirmed material; it will not contain invented recipes, salt percentages, batch dates or handwriting.

On desktop, the log occupies a large, sticky area beside readable text. The full sequence takes roughly nine to ten screen heights, with ordinary scrolling and no forced stops. All six leaves remain present, sometimes gathered behind the active one.

**1. Started — arrival**

The first screen establishes:

- Ines Okafor.
- Head Chef at Saltmarsh, Leeds.
- Your focus on fermentation, whole-vegetable cooking and apprentices.
- The question that guides the page.
- A compact piece of evidence: the whole kitchen’s reduction from 14 to 5 kg of waste per week, with its one-month 2023 measurement scope alongside it.

The log begins open, slightly staggered, with enough depth to feel physical. Its first leaf introduces your influences: your grandmother, *The Art of Fermentation* and *Wild Fermentation*. Your photograph of the ogiri pot can sit here once supplied. The opening does not invent a family story around it.

**What moves:** the leaves gently separate as the visitor begins scrolling, revealing the document’s structure.

**What visitors can click:** direct routes to workshops, apprentice enquiries and writer enquiries; chapter navigation; and a skip-to-contact link. Nobody needs to complete the animation to reach you.

**2. Started — background**

The second part of this chapter gives a short, accurate account of your background rather than a full employment-history section.

It includes the ten-week unpaid stage at Fjaerland: washing jars, labelling them and helping with two batches of garum. Your Saltmarsh dates distinguish acting head chef from March 2022 and Head Chef from September 2022.

**What moves:** three leaves form a compact sequence of influences and dated experience. The influence leaf stays visually separate from the timeline, avoiding an invented chronology.

**What visitors can click:** an accessible “Background” disclosure for the additional details. Essential identity and role information remain visible without opening it.

**3. Salt — how the work is recorded**

This chapter makes the ferment log understandable through its actual fields:

- Date started.
- Salt.
- Days checked.
- Ready.

The prep list appears alongside it as the other document you work from. This section explains the structure of your records without pretending to reproduce a real batch.

**What moves:** four leaves align into fields, a fifth holds the prep-list reference, and the sixth remains gathered at the edge. The arrangement makes the relationship between the fields visible.

**What visitors can click:** each field can be selected or focused to highlight its corresponding explanation. All explanations also remain readable in the page; this interaction is optional.

**4. Checks — practice, apprentices and writing**

The narrative widens from the record itself to your apprentice programme and *Brine*.

The content establishes that you run the programme and write about preserving. It does not invent a curriculum, apprentice outcomes or current vacancies. *Brine* appears through its title and confirmed subject matter; scans containing Olu’s drawings stay out until he agrees.

**What moves:** the six leaves pair into three working spreads: checking, apprentices and writing. Their arrangement connects these activities without claiming that your teaching follows a particular unconfirmed method.

**What visitors can click:** short text details about the programme and *Brine*, plus an apprentice-enquiry link. A publication link can be added if a real destination is available.

**5. Ready — work in view**

This is the most photographic part of the page.

Your own larder photographs provide the main material. A wider view establishes the space; a detail can show labels or texture after checking for sensitive information. Text entries alongside the photographs cover the larder, apprentice programme, *Brine* and workshops.

This is a work index, not six invented projects. If only a few photographs are suitable, the remaining leaves carry type.

**What moves:** the leaves spread into a loose contact sheet. The active image becomes larger while the others remain visible. There is no separate animated jar wall or cupboard scene.

**What visitors can click:** photographs open at a useful size, with credits and descriptions. The image viewer supports keyboard controls, Escape to close and return to the originating image. A workshop link jumps directly to the closing contact section.

Workshop dates, venue, booking details and availability will come from current information before launch.

**6. Review — the measured result**

The evidence gets a quiet, readable moment:

| Measure | Treatment |
|---|---|
| 14 kg → 5 kg per week | Show the raw figures clearly |
| Attribution | Whole kitchen; use “we” |
| Measurement | Weighed over one month in 2023 |
| Included | Prep and plate waste |
| Excluded | Bones, because they went to stock |

The page will not extrapolate annual savings, imply that this is a current measurement, or attribute the result solely to you or the ferment log.

**What moves:** two leaves square themselves towards the visitor, displaying the two values at equal typographic scale. The remaining leaves stay gathered nearby. Numbers do not count up or down.

**What visitors can click:** no interaction is required to understand the result. Its measurement note remains visible rather than hidden behind a tooltip.

**7. Review — Callum’s words**

The next settled moment presents the approved quotation:

> “Ines turned our bins into a larder. The best thing on the menu most weeks started as something we used to throw away.”

Attribution: Callum Reyes, owner of Saltmarsh.

**What moves:** the quotation leaf comes forward, with the measurement leaves still visible behind it.

**What visitors can click:** the normal chapter and contact navigation. There is no testimonial carousel or additional interaction to learn.

**8. Next batch — the menu and the invitation**

The ending completes the question from the opening: preparation and recorded checks come before readiness, and the menu is written last.

The final leaf introduces the menu’s place in that sequence. It does not display invented dishes.

**What moves:** the leaves gather back into one open log. The final leaf turns once and rests. The scene is still while visitors decide what to do.

**What visitors can click:**

1. **Workshops:** booking through your real booking destination, or an enquiry route until one exists.
2. **Apprenticeships:** an enquiry route without implying that recruitment is currently open.
3. **Writing enquiries:** a clear contact route for food writers.

The footer provides credits, relevant privacy information and a return-to-start link.

**The visual design**

The chosen look is warm working paper with precise printed information.

| Element | Choice |
|---|---|
| Page ground | Warm paper, `#F2EBDD` |
| Main ink | Near-black, `#242821` |
| Accent | Dark olive, `#495B38` |
| Log leaves | Almost-white, `#FFFCF4` |
| Surface | Fine rules, restrained grain, shallow shadows |

**Source Serif 4** handles headings and reading text. **IBM Plex Mono** handles log fields, dates, measurements and small navigation labels. Both can be self-hosted.

The layout gives prose comfortable line lengths and generous space. Important information never depends on reading tiny lettering on a tilted 3D surface. Photographs retain their own character rather than receiving a heavy colour treatment.

Movement consists of modest turns, shifts and regrouping. Each arrangement settles before its text needs attention. There is no automatic sound, cursor-following camera or scroll hijacking.

**Navigation and interaction throughout**

A discreet desktop rail names the six chapters: Started, Salt, Checks, Ready, Review and Next batch. On phones, this becomes a compact chapter menu.

Chapter links use ordinary page anchors. Browser back, keyboard navigation and direct links to sections work normally. Hover can emphasise an element, but never reveals information unavailable by touch or keyboard.

**On a phone and without 3D**

| Situation | What the visitor gets |
|---|---|
| **Phone** | The same complete story, using static two-dimensional log leaves above the text. Photographs stack naturally, contact buttons are large, and sections take only the space their content needs. |
| **Reduced motion** | Settled compositions with no leaf turns, camera movement, parallax or animated numbers. |
| **No WebGL, or graphics failure** | Static log illustrations replace the scene. Text, photographs, links and scroll position remain usable. |
| **No JavaScript** | Complete HTML content, static illustrations, ordinary chapter links and working contact destinations. |
| **Screen reader** | A properly ordered document with headings, image descriptions and every fact represented in text. The duplicate canvas scene is ignored. |

The default phone experience does not load the 3D engine. This keeps the page lighter and avoids compressing a desktop animation into a small screen.

The future implementation should support visible keyboard focus, strong contrast, zoom, touch targets of at least 44 pixels and no colour-only meanings.

**Everything else the site needs**

“Include” below describes the eventual implementation scope, not work being built now.

| Item | Decision |
|---|---|
| Chapter navigation and contact shortcuts | **Include**, available from the opening |
| Work index | **Include** larder, apprentices, *Brine* and workshops using confirmed material |
| Individual project pages | **Later**, when there is enough cleared content |
| Sunday Pot feature | **Later**, once your particular contribution and story boundaries are established |
| Contact and booking | **Include** real destinations; prefer an existing booking service |
| CV | **Omit** from this scope; you are not job seeking |
| Testimonial | **Include** Callum’s approved quotation |
| Languages | **English initially** |
| Search presentation | **Include** page title, description, canonical address and sitemap |
| Shared-link image | **Include** a log-derived composition with your name and role |
| Site icon | **Include** a simple mark derived from the log’s ruling |
| Missing-address page | **Include** useful links back to the page and contact |
| Image credits | **Include**, beside images where appropriate and in a compact credits area |
| Privacy and legal information | **Include as applicable** to the eventual operator and services |
| Analytics | **Omit nonessential tracking by default** |
| Blog | **Later**; no empty publishing section |
| Chat | **Omit** |
| Editing | **Include** a simple way to maintain workshop links, contact details and credits; defer a separate CMS |
| Domain and hosting | **Plan for** an owner-controlled domain, HTTPS and reproducible deployment; no provider or expenditure chosen |
| Maintenance | **Include** a short update guide and source/asset backups |
| Verification | **Include at build stage** keyboard, phone, zoom, fallback, contrast, link and performance checks |

Readable content should load first, with desktop 3D added afterwards. Images should be appropriately sized and compressed, and rendering should stop when the scene is offscreen. Performance targets are a main-content load under 2.5 seconds and minimal layout movement on representative mobile testing; these are future targets, not measured results.

**Assumptions and materials still needed**

I chose the log over prep slips and tags, the paper-and-olive palette, static mobile presentation, and workshop enquiries as the first contact priority. These are design decisions made under your delegation.

Before an eventual launch, the remaining inputs are:

- Your actual personal photographs, checked for supplier prices and unapproved staff faces.
- Real public contact and workshop destinations.
- Final narrative copy grounded in the confirmed facts.
- Domain and hosting arrangements.
- Restaurant reuse permission if Priya’s photographs are included, with her credit.
- Olu’s permission before including his drawings or scans containing them.

The core plan works without either set of third-party artwork. Unconfirmed counts, detailed claims about earlier roles and invented family or project stories remain excluded.

The supporting [facts](/tmp/storyfolio-evals/codex-chef-with-0bOu0J/docs/story/facts.md), [design decisions](/tmp/storyfolio-evals/codex-chef-with-0bOu0J/docs/story/decided-for-you.md) and [handover](/tmp/storyfolio-evals/codex-chef-with-0bOu0J/docs/story/handover.md) are saved alongside the storyboard. Building is outside this planning phase, and no implementation or publication has occurred.
